Standard: The air vehicle is no worse than Level 2 handling qualities during waveoff from a carrier approach. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct analysis of shore-based and shipboard carrier waveoff, while maintaining heading control over the landing area and the minimum hook to carrier ramp and deck clearance, to determine the control power, roll and flight path control power and bandwidth, power and engine response, margin to stall speed, and defined minimum and maximum approach airspeed and flight path angle needed to complete the mission task, including 6-DOF simulations for automatic control modes, for each combination of air vehicle states, control modes, environmental conditions, and ship conditions: ship class and arresting gear layout, WOD magnitude and direction, steady and turbulence carrier airwake and ship motion effects, ship speed and turn rate, subject to the constraints of the arresting gear capabilities and airframe structural limits (for a successful arrestment). Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct piloted simulation and evaluation of land-based and shipboard carrier waveoff as specified in SA FTM-01, Landing Tests section for each combination of air vehicle states, control modes, including reversionary modes, environmental conditions, and ship conditions: ship class and arresting gear layout, approach speed, flight path angle, WOD magnitude and direction, steady and turbulence carrier airwake and ship motion effects, ship speed and turn rate, subject to the constraints of the arresting gear capabilities and airframe structural limits (for a successful arrestment). Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct shore-based carrier approach-style waveoffs as specified in SA FTM-01, Landing Tests section for nominal and critical combinations of air vehicle states, control modes, including reversionary modes, environmental conditions, and ship conditions: arresting gear type and layout, approach speed, flight path angle, headwind and crosswind conditions from minimum to maximum shore-based WOD equivalent, subject to the constraints of the arresting gear capabilities and airframe structural limits (for a successful arrestment).
  (3) Flight test: Conduct shipboard waveoffs as specified in SA FTM-01, Landing Tests section for nominal and critical combinations of air vehicle states, control modes, including reversionary modes, environmental conditions, and ship conditions: arresting gear type and shipboard layout/configuration, approach speed, flight path angle, multiple levels of ship motion, WOD magnitudes and directions from minimum to maximum WOD, subject to the constraints of the arresting gear capabilities and airframe structural limits (for a successful arrestment).
